verification.note: docs/reference/api.md:188 still says 'a re-upload over a trashed file at that path replaces the ghost and gets a new record'. backend/app/services/upload.py:151-152 makes init_upload raise 409 'File already exists' whenever target_full exists on disk, and nothing there checks the trash state. Trash is a soft delete that leaves the file on disk: backend/tests/test_inbox_arrival.py:147-160 deletes a file, uploads to the same path, and gets 409 with the old content still in place. The ghost-purge branch at upload.py:317-326 is reached only when the trashed file's bytes are already gone, and test_trashed_ghost_is_replaced_and_gets_a_new_row (test_inbox_arrival.py:129-144) sets that up with an explicit unlink at line 135. In normal use the documented replacement does not happen, so the doc sentence is wrong. The api.md row for upload/init (line 186) does not mention this 409 either.

specification_compliance: The code (upload.py:151) and the tests (test_inbox_arrival.py:147) agree that an upload over a trashed file still on disk is refused with 409. Only the API reference row at api.md:188 says otherwise.
regression_risks: A reader who relies on api.md:188 would expect a re-upload over a trashed file to succeed, but init answers 409.
test_coverage: test_upload_over_a_trashed_file_still_on_disk_is_refused covers the 409 both with and without inbox_source; test_trashed_ghost_is_replaced_and_gets_a_new_row covers ghost replacement when the trashed file's bytes are gone from disk.
not_verified: I did not run the tests; I verified by reading the code only.
